answers.answer: Give each player a Clover board and marker. Shuffle the Keyword cards into a face-down deck within everyone’s reach. Each player draws 4 cards and places them randomly in the board’s recessed spots, keeping them hidden from others.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Give each player a Clover board and marker’; shuffle into a face-down deck; draw 4 and place randomly; ‘Keep your cards hidden.’

answers.answer: The phases are Choosing Clues, then Resolution. During Choosing Clues, everyone works individually, simultaneously and secretly. The two Keywords below each Clue Zone form one Pair, making four Pairs.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Choosing Clues: everyone works individually, simultaneously and secretly.’ Actions: ‘The 2 Keywords below each Clue Zone form a Pair: there are four Pairs.’

answers.answer: A Clue must be one single word; compound words are allowed. Permitted forms are a common noun, proper noun, acronym, number, or onomatopoeia.
answers.evidence: Actions—Choosing Clues: ‘A Clue must be a single word; compound words are allowed. It may be a common noun, proper noun, acronym, number or onomatopoeia.’

answers.answer: No. A Clue cannot be either Keyword itself.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: ‘Either Keyword itself, or its translation into another language.’

answers.answer: No. Amour is a translation of Love, and a Clue cannot be either Keyword’s translation into another language.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues gives the example: ‘Amour cannot connect Love and France.’

answers.answer: No. Prince is in the same word family as Princess, which is an invalid Clue.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: ‘A word in the same family as a Keyword: Prince cannot connect Princess and Brother.’

answers.answer: No. Cuppajo is a made-up word, and made-up words are invalid Clues.
answers.evidence: Invalid Clues: ‘A made-up word: Cuppajo cannot connect Mug and Morning.’

answers.answer: Each player writes 4 Clues, one for each Pair, and each Clue must connect both Keywords in that Pair. Write each in its corresponding Clue Zone.
answers.evidence: Actions—Choosing Clues: ‘For each Pair, write one Clue connecting both Keywords in the corresponding Clue Zone. Write 4 Clues in total.’

answers.answer: Remove all 4 Keyword cards, draw 1 new card without looking at it, shuffle it with the 4 removed cards, then put the board down with the 5 cards in a face-down pile on top. The added card may not be inspected when drawn.
answers.evidence: After writing all four Clues: remove all four cards; ‘Draw 1 new card without looking at it’; shuffle with those four; place the 5-card face-down pile on the board.

answers.answer: Resolution starts only after everyone has finished the preparation steps.
answers.evidence: Actions—Choosing Clues: ‘Start Resolution only after everyone has finished these steps.’

answers.answer: The first Spectator is chosen when Resolution begins. The other players look at that board and work together to reconstruct its original Pairs using the written Clues. The Spectator cannot communicate in any way, including spoken hints or gestures.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Choose the first Spectator when Resolution begins’; all other players work together; the Spectator ‘cannot communicate in any way,’ including speech, hints or gestures.

answers.answer: The Spectator places their Clover board and all 5 cards face up in the middle of the table. The others use the four Clues to put the four original cards into their correct spaces and orientations, leaving the extra card off the board.
answers.evidence: Resolution and verification: the Spectator puts the board and all 5 cards ‘face up in the middle’; others reconstruct the original Pairs, place four original cards correctly and leave the extra off it.

answers.answer: The player to the Spectator’s left makes the final decision.
answers.evidence: Resolution and verification: ‘If they disagree about placement, the player to the Spectator’s left makes the final decision.’

answers.answer: Yes. Guessers may discuss their reasoning and physically try card arrangements. Once they agree on a placement, the Spectator verifies it.
answers.evidence: Resolution and verification: guessers ‘may discuss their reasoning and physically try card arrangements’; ‘Once they agree on a placement, the Spectator verifies it.’

answers.answer: The team scores 6 points: 1 point for each of the 4 correct cards plus a 2-point first-try bonus. The board is resolved, so no second attempt is needed.
answers.evidence: ‘First attempt, all Pairs correct: score 6 points: 1 per card (4) plus a 2-point first-try bonus. The board is resolved; no second attempt is needed.’

answers.answer: The Spectator silently removes the incorrect card(s) and puts them in the middle of the table. They may not explain the mistake or otherwise communicate during Resolution. The team receives one second and final attempt.
answers.evidence: On a first-attempt error, the Spectator ‘silently removes the incorrect card(s)’ and puts them in the middle; others get a ‘second and final attempt.’ Special Rules: they may not explain or otherwise communicate.

answers.answer: The score is 4 points, one per correct card remaining. The first-try bonus is not awarded.
answers.evidence: Second attempt: score ‘1 point per correct card remaining,’ 0–4 points, ‘with no first-try bonus’; a perfect second-attempt board is worth 4.

answers.answer: The Spectator removes the incorrect card to the middle of the table. The team scores 3 points, one per correct card remaining, and there is no third attempt.
answers.evidence: Second attempt: the Spectator removes any incorrect cards to the middle; score 1 per correct card remaining; ‘There is no third attempt.’

answers.answer: The Spectator turns the board over and writes its points in the middle. All 5 used cards are discarded. The player to the Spectator’s left becomes the next Spectator.
answers.evidence: After resolving the board: ‘turns it over, writes its points in the middle, and discards all 5 used Keyword cards. The player to their left becomes the next Spectator.’

answers.answer: The game ends after every player has been Spectator once; each player is Spectator exactly once. Add all points written on the boards, record the team total in the Record of Legends, and try to beat the previous high score.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Each player is Spectator exactly once per game.’ Scoring / Victory Conditions: after every player has been Spectator once, add all points, record the team total in the Record of Legends, and try to beat the previous high score.
